key_insight: A geometrically exact planar beam formulation can incorporate hyperelasticity cleanly by separating in-plane kinematics from out-of-plane constitutive reduction, with plane stress giving the most robust global response.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical beam-modeling route for structural analysis when full 3D solids are too costly but material nonlinearity and thickness effects still matter.
method: Start from a conventional three-field geometrically exact planar beam model with linear elasticity.
Enrich kinematics with a global in-plane thickness deformation field.
Treat the out-of-plane behavior separately using plane-stress or plane-strain constitutive reductions for hyperelastic laws.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks in the abstract show that plane-stress gives nearly identical centerline deformations across the Poisson's ratios considered, while plane-strain becomes noticeably stiffer as Poisson's ratio increases.
watch_item: Plane-strain reduction can introduce strong Poisson-ratio sensitivity and over-stiffening, so constitutive reduction choice must match the intended physical setting.
paper_title: On finite elements for geometrically-exact planar beams with hyperelastic material models
